hypotheses: Legitimate cardholder behavior: The customer is making an unusual online purchase (product R) from a desktop computer, representing a benign channel shift.
Account Takeover (ATO) / Card-Not-Present (CNP) Fraud: An unauthorized user has compromised the card details and is transacting online with a new device and email.

events.msg: Four specialist analysts reviewing their evidence in parallel

events.assessment: The flagged online transaction (3509359) represents a significant departure from the customer's historical baseline, which is predominantly in-person (78 out of 82 transactions). It was conducted via a new device profile that, despite being flagged as non-generic, has been associated with 462 other transactions across the system, strongly suggesting a shared device or fraud ring environment.
key_points: Transaction 3509359 ($125.08) is an online purchase of product type R, whereas the customer's baseline consists of 95% in-person transactions (78 out of 82) and primarily product type W.

The transaction was initiated from a 'New' device profile ('Trident/7.0 | Windows 10 | ie 11.0 for desktop | 1920x1080') that is not generic but has a high velocity of 462 transactions across the system.

The real-time risk score flagged this transaction at 0.52, while the transaction model (model_p) scored it low at 0.010351, highlighting a discrepancy between real-time risk indicators and historical model training.
